conclusion: rdbg_open now validates both qcom_smem_get results before publishing or dereferencing the shared-memory pointer. The stock binary has an unchecked ERR_PTR path for errors other than -ENOENT; the new code preserves the provider errno and returns before check_subsystem_debug_enabled.

findings.description: Stock checks IS_ERR after the common qcom_smem_get call, falls back only for -ENOENT, then checks only NULL before using the pointer. The pinned target qcom_smem_get can return ERR_PTR(-EPROBE_DEFER) when __smem is unavailable and ERR_PTR(-EINVAL) for an invalid item. Such a pointer reaches check_subsystem_debug_enabled in stock. The candidate stores the result locally, performs the device-specific fallback only for -ENOENT, checks IS_ERR after either call, returns PTR_ERR on failure, checks NULL, and only then publishes rdbgdata->smem_addr.
Probe publication and open snapshot use the same mutex; free_irq uses the per-open requested IRQ.
The module-owned SMEM state handle replacement and use remain serialized by rdbg_smem_state_lock.
